title: Fall / Autumn
summary: Fall was a season of harvest, storage, hunting, and preparation. Corn, beans, squash, nuts, and other foods could be gathered and processed for the colder months. Sources also describe fall and winter as important hunting seasons, when deer and other animals provided meat, hides, sinew, bone, and other materials.
content:
Storage was part of seasonal knowledge. Food could be dried, smoked, placed in pits, or otherwise protected for winter use. English observers called some storage pits "Indian barns," but those words should be understood as colonial descriptions of Native food-storage technology, not as simple farm buildings.

Fall also connects to gratitude and community gathering. Project sources link harvest-time ceremonies and later public celebrations to continuing Native community life. Pages about food, ecology, and continued Indigenous presence should show fall as both seasonal preparation and living cultural continuity.

Related pages: Ecology and Flexible Sedentism, Food, Fishing, Shell Midden, Wampum, Continued Indigenous Presence Today.
